cases.surface: HTTP API in Node, with routes, an ORM-less query helper, templates and an outbound fetch
single-file command-line tool in Python: archives, temporary files, subprocesses, a credential on disk
Terraform root and network module, plus two GitHub Actions workflows
published Node CLI: manifest, install scripts, registry configuration, vendored helper, runtime config
support assistant with retrieval, tools, persistent memory and an MCP configuration
billing analytics service: serializers, logging, an LLM summarizer and lifecycle jobs

planted.class: object-level authorization missing
planted.why_it_is_real: The id is bound and nothing scopes the row to the caller, so any session reads any invoice.

planted.class: SQL injection through an interpolated ORDER BY
planted.why_it_is_real: req.query.order is concatenated into the statement; parameters cannot bind a column.

planted.class: server-side request forgery
planted.why_it_is_real: The URL comes from the body and fetchLogo follows redirects with no allowlist. The defect spans two files: the route that accepts the URL and the helper that fetches it, so a finding at either location is the same finding.

planted.class: self-contained token decoded, never verified
planted.why_it_is_real: jwt.decode does not check the signature and the claims decide the role.

planted.class: cross-site scripting in server-side rendering
planted.why_it_is_real: The note is interpolated into HTML with no escaping at the sink.

planted.class: path traversal through archive extraction
planted.why_it_is_real: extractall with no filter and no prefix re-check writes wherever the entry names point.

planted.class: predictable temporary file in a shared directory
planted.why_it_is_real: The name is derived from the pid inside /tmp, so another local user can pre-create it.

planted.class: argument injection into a subprocess
planted.why_it_is_real: The path reaches gpg with no -- terminator, so a value starting with - is read as an option.

planted.class: untrusted search path
planted.why_it_is_real: A bare binary name is resolved through the inherited PATH in a tool documented to run under sudo.

planted.class: credential written with the ambient umask in a shared directory
planted.why_it_is_real: The token lands in /tmp with default modes, readable by other local users.

planted.class: IAM policy with a wildcard action on every resource
planted.why_it_is_real: Action "*" on Resource "*" with no condition, attached to a workload role.

planted.class: public access block disabled on a bucket holding billing reports
planted.why_it_is_real: All four block settings are false, so an ACL or policy can expose the objects.

planted.class: database storage not encrypted at rest
planted.why_it_is_real: storage_encrypted = false on the store that holds billing data.

planted.class: SSH open to the whole internet
planted.why_it_is_real: Port 22 with cidr_blocks 0.0.0.0/0 on the bastion group.

planted.class: privileged trigger checking out untrusted PR code
planted.why_it_is_real: pull_request_target checks out the PR head SHA and then runs the PR's own build.

planted.class: GITHUB_TOKEN with write-all on a workflow reachable from a fork
planted.why_it_is_real: permissions: write-all combined with the privileged trigger above.

planted.class: arbitrary code fetched at install time with no integrity check
planted.why_it_is_real: A preinstall script downloads a binary over the network and chmods it into /usr/local/bin, with no digest and no signature. The URL, the destination and the chmod live in main(); the helper is the write.

planted.class: live credential committed to the working tree
planted.why_it_is_real: A token with a live-looking prefix sits in a versioned configuration file.

planted.class: install-time lifecycle script in a published package
planted.why_it_is_real: preinstall runs on every consumer's machine before anything is reviewed.

planted.class: dependency whose name is one transposition from a popular package
planted.why_it_is_real: lodahs is a character transposition of lodash and is pinned as a direct dependency.

planted.class: binary artifact committed to the source tree with no recipe
planted.why_it_is_real: A binary the CLI shells out to is versioned in the repository and its own README says it is not the output of any recipe here.

planted.class: retrieved content interpolated into the prompt with no delimitation or provenance
planted.why_it_is_real: Documents are joined into the same string as the system instructions and the question.

planted.class: authorization decided by the model's output
planted.why_it_is_real: The account id the tool acts on comes from the model's decision, not from the session.

planted.class: free-text write into persistent memory from model output
planted.why_it_is_real: Whatever the model produced is appended to a store that later runs feed back in.

planted.class: model output reaching a shell
planted.why_it_is_real: subprocess.run with shell=True on a string the model produced.

planted.class: secret in cleartext in an MCP configuration file
planted.why_it_is_real: The API key is a literal in the config rather than a reference to a manager.

planted.class: MCP server installed from a moving tag
planted.why_it_is_real: npx -y with @latest resolves to whatever was published most recently, at every start.

planted.class: ingestion with no origin or trust metadata
planted.why_it_is_real: Customer ticket bodies are indexed with nothing recording where they came from.

planted.class: serializer returns every field of the model
planted.why_it_is_real: national_id, internal_risk_score and support_notes reach the dashboard response.

planted.class: personal data written to the application log
planted.why_it_is_real: Email and national id are formatted into every request log line.

planted.class: identifiable personal data sent to a model provider
planted.why_it_is_real: Name, email and national id are interpolated into the prompt.

planted.class: third-party tags loaded with no consent gate
planted.why_it_is_real: Two third-party scripts are rendered unconditionally.

decoys.why: The query is scoped to req.user.id in the statement itself.
The interpolated column comes from a closed map, never from the request.
decode() feeds a metric label; authorization is resolved from the server-side session.
escapeHtml is applied at the sink.
The only interpolated value is Number(year); nothing external reaches it.
Host allowlist checked after parsing, with redirects disabled.
extractall(filter="data") rejects traversal and absolute names.
mkdtemp plus mkstemp: atomic, exclusive, inside a directory this process created.
The -- terminator is present and the path must already resolve.
0600 inside a 0700 per-user directory.
rmtree runs on a directory this process created in this run.
Scoped to two actions on one bucket prefix with an aws:ResourceAccount condition.
Read is granted to a CloudFront origin access identity, not to the world, and the object is marketing content.
443 open on an internet-facing load balancer is the point; the finding moves to what sits behind it.
The commit message travels through env: and is referenced as a quoted shell variable.
The action is pinned by commit SHA with persist-credentials disabled.
The download is verified against a pinned sha256 and the build refuses to continue on mismatch.
A template file whose values are placeholders and a documented test-mode key prefix.
Explicit scope mapping sends @acme to the internal registry, so a public package cannot take the name.
Small, functionally complete package with no recent release: assess issues and maintainer, do not report age alone.
Documents travel as separate blocks carrying origin and trust, delimited from the question.
The account id comes from the authenticated session and refunds are refused outright.
Only keys from a closed schema are stored, with a ttl.
The operation must be one of a closed set and nothing is executed.
The value is a ${VAR} substitution placeholder, not a secret.
Every indexed chunk carries origin and trust metadata that retrieval filters on.
An explicit field allowlist with a test that fails when a new field appears.
Only an opaque identifier is logged, and a redacting formatter covers anything else.
Identifiers are replaced by reversible tokens before the prompt is built.
Tags load only for the categories the visitor accepted.
The purge covers every store in the inventory, not only the primary.
